title: Sheet and board differ: R21 is fitted the other way round and renamed on the sheet (0 ohm link) after the last ECO

title: R10 exists on the sheets but the board's R10 footprint is not linked to it
detail: the board component at (29.10, 69.80) has no SOURCEDESIGNATOR / unique id (a free part whose silkscreen text says R10); the next Update PCB adds a second R10. Nets NetR10_1 / NetR7_1 are correct

title: D6: sheet/BOM says BAS31, board says BAT54SLT1G
detail: the BOM orders the sheet's part; the board's comment is what an assembler reading the P&P sees. D6: the board's BAT54S (Schottky) conducts 2 uA at 100 mV and ~0.3 mA at 250 mV through the 20 ohm sense resistors; the sheet's BAS31 (silicon) does not - the silicon part must be the one fitted

title: R2: sheet/BOM says ERA-6VRW8201V, board says RR1220P-8251-D-M
detail: the BOM orders the sheet's part; the board's comment is what an assembler reading the P&P sees. R2/R9: RR1220P-8251-D-M is 8.25 k 0.5 %, the sheet's ERA-6VRW8201V is 8.2 k 0.05 %; the difference amplifier ratio moves 0.6 % between them

title: R9: sheet/BOM says ERA-6VRW8201V, board says RR1220P-8251-D-M
detail: the BOM orders the sheet's part; the board's comment is what an assembler reading the P&P sees. R2/R9: RR1220P-8251-D-M is 8.25 k 0.5 %, the sheet's ERA-6VRW8201V is 8.2 k 0.05 %; the difference amplifier ratio moves 0.6 % between them

title: Barrier creepage 3.43 mm (bottom) / 3.68 mm (top) around the slot's left end, below the 4.0 mm basic figure for 400 V
detail: shortest surface path from the GND_ISO / +5_ISO pours at (25.3-25.6, 43.9) round the slot tip to the +5 pour that wraps into the bridge at (23.7, 46.5). IEC 60664-1 table F.5, PD2, material group IIIb: 4.0 mm basic / 8.0 mm reinforced at 400 V (5.0 mm at 500 V); the DC-DC module's own creepage is 4.0 mm. Supported working voltage at 3.43 mm is about 340 V basic

title: Aluminium case rail (bonded to ISenseRTN) is 3.60 mm from PSU1's -Vout pad along the bottom surface at 1 mm groove engagement
detail: the right-hand rail lands next to the isolated secondary at the slot's right end; 4.1 mm at 0.5 mm engagement, 2.6 mm at 2.0 mm. Anodising is a film, not rated insulation (trap 1). Engagement depth is on no drawing

title: Free 3.5 mm plated hole at (21.75, 43.0) sits 2.1 mm from measured-side copper and 1.8 mm from output-side copper
detail: no net, no component; a metal fastener in it bridges the barrier at 2.1 mm. Its purpose is not recorded

title: Pours on every layer come within 0.21 mm of the slot wall
detail: GND (inner planes), +5, +12 and GND_ISO / +5_ISO all stop 0.21-0.22 mm from the routed slot; routing tolerance is of that order, so inner copper can be exposed in the slot. The clearance across the 2.5 mm slot itself is adequate

title: No design rule enforces the barrier
detail: the exported rule set has one 0.200 mm clearance rule scoped to the whole board; a clearance rule between a measured-side net class and everything else at 4.0 mm (and 0.5 mm pour-to-cutout) would have caught both findings above

title: J2's 400 V rating applies to overvoltage category II / pollution degree 2 only
detail: 5442002 catalog: 400 V (II/2), 320 V (III/2), 250 V (III/3), 4 kV surge, material group I. SAFETY.md quotes 400 V without the category

title: x100 full scale (5.0 V) is at the output clamp at 13 V in: two Schottky drops plus the regulator dropout
detail: headroom -0.01 V typical, -0.41 V at the guaranteed 14.5 V regulator input; full scale is reachable above 13.05 V (typ) / 13.85 V (guaranteed). Regulation thresholds at the jack: x10 14.06 / 14.86 V, x100 14.42 / 15.22 V (typ / guaranteed)

title: U6 (HT7550-1, SOT-89) dissipates 0.62 W at 15 V and 0.71 W at 16 V against a 0.5 W package rating
detail: 63 mA of module input (the measured 95.8 mA total less everything else, implying 43 % module efficiency at 14 % load) plus 3.5 mA for the Si8921 from VregIn 14.3-15.6 V. Simulated hotspot 76 C in free air at 25 C, 107 C in the case at 40 C (operating range of the part is 85 C ambient, 150 C junction)

title: SW1 carries 93-97 % of its 0.1 A rating at 15 V (rated 12 V) and makes/breaks the board supply
detail: pole terminal 2 confirmed from the C&K table (1-2, 2-3, 2-4); 10,000-cycle life; switching into C3 (22 uF) from the 1176 uF input bank

title: Relay coil at 16 V is 130 % of rating, within the G6L's 150 % maximum to 70 C
detail: corrects finding 15: the 13-16 V silkscreen is not what limits the input; U6 dissipation is (0.71 W at 16 V)

title: The slot makes the shunt area a thermal island: R5 at 10 A reaches 110 C in free air and 138 C in the case at 40 C with 2.5 mm2 leads as fins
detail: without the leads the model gives 192-325 C, so the shunt is cooled by its wiring. At +85 C the shunt's 50 ppm/C is a 0.4 % gain term on the 10 A range (the budget assumed a 33 C rise); the Si8921 input side sits at 68-95 C. Measure the shunt at 10 A with the real leads, or derate the continuous current on the x10 range

title: J2-to-shunt pours rise ~21 C at 10 A (IPC-2221, 1 oz, top layer only)
detail: 4.55 mm wide; a second copper layer or 2 oz halves it

title: U9_x100 loop: phase margin 26 deg (simulated, LM7321 model at its 10 V group)
detail: Tian probe at the amplifier output with the board's loads (22 uF derated on the references); crossover 3.74e+04 Hz. The LM7321 is specified for unlimited capacitive load and the bench board shows no instability, so this is a question about the model's output stage, not a fault found: confirm with a step on DiffAmpRef

title: x100 bandwidth is set by C9 (47 nF) against the 50 ohm output resistors: simulated 58 kHz, measured 60 kHz
detail: C9 is switched to board GND by Q6 on the x100 range; C8 (680 pF) with R32 (1 k) adds a 234 kHz pole. x10: 575 kHz simulated against 580 kHz measured, set by the Si8921

title: Input-referred noise 1.7 mA rms (x100, 60 kHz) and 5.4 mA rms (x10, 580 kHz), dominated by the Si8921
detail: bench: ~2 mA rms on x100; the x10 bench figure (12 mA rms) is a 108 kHz spur, not the noise floor

title: LM7321 bias current (0.4 uA typ, up to 2 uA) through the R21 asymmetry: 4 mV typ / 20 mV max offset between the two references with the board's 10 k, zero with the sheet's 0 R
detail: simulated with the vendor model (Ib -1.1 uA): DiffAmpRef - ISenseRTN = +11.1 mV with 10 k, -0.05 mV with 0 R, against a +/-3 mV trim span. A 10 k R21 can put the zero out of reach on a worst-case LM7321; the sheet's 0 R (or 100 R) removes it. The datasheet figure is ten times the 50 nA the previous review assumed

title: D6 as drawn is an antiparallel clamp across AIP/AIN (+/-0.7 V with BAS31), not a series pair
detail: pins 1 and 2 on AIN, pin 3 on AIP. The Si8921 absolute maximum is -0.5 V / VDDA + 0.5 V, so the clamp protects; with the board's BAT54S it also leaks 0.3 mA at the 250 mV input maximum (2.4 % of full scale through the 20 ohm) - see bom-2

title: Pours come within 0.21 mm of the barrier slot wall on every layer
detail: JLC routed-edge copper clearance is 0.30 mm; a 0.2 mm setback can leave inner-layer copper exposed in the slot after routing tolerance

title: Barrier slot is drawn on the Outline layer as a 2.5 mm stroked path, not a closed cut-out contour
detail: D103 C,2.5: a fab reading the profile layer must interpret a wide stroke as a routed slot; the saved board carries it as a board cut-out region, so an ODB++/IPC-2581 export or a drawn contour removes the ambiguity

title: A .GKO (keep-out) file with an 11.5 x 3.9 mm rectangle is in the fabrication set
detail: fabs that take GKO as the profile when present would cut the wrong board; the keep-out region under U2 should not be output, or the file dropped from the order zip

title: No fiducials and no test points on the board
detail: a 95-part double-sided board going to machine assembly needs two or three fiducials per side; the only probe points are component pads

title: Conducted emission at the 15 V port from PSU1: worst margin -4.8 dB to CISPR 32 Class B AVG (10-30 MHz), module scan de-embedded
detail: common-mode current through the 2.5 pF barrier, CM1 buys ~1 dB against a 40 kohm source; the Si8921 modulator and the real earth path of the measured circuit are not in the estimate. A LISN scan settles it
